topic: Grover's Algorithm: The Quantum Needle in a Haystack
target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science students and tech enthusiasts

sections.title: The Search Dilemma: Classical vs. Quantum
lecture_lines: Finding one item in N takes N/2 classical tries.
For 1,000 items, that's about 500 attempts.
Quantum search needs only about 32 tries.
This speedup is known as Grover's Algorithm.
It scales with the square root of N.
animations: Display text 'Classical Search: O(N)' and a grid [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] of 100 white squares (#FFFFFF) representing N items.
Sequentially highlight 50 squares [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg] in red (#FF0000) one by one to demonstrate the average number of classical tries.
Clear highlights; display 'Quantum Search: O(√N)' in green (#00FF00) at the top of the screen.
Animate a single fast cyan scan line (#00FFFF) passing across the entire grid [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] to represent quantum parallel processing.
Highlight a single target square [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg] in bright green (#00FF00) and show the formula '√1000 ≈ 32' next to it.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Superposition and State Representation
lecture_lines: Quantum computers search all possibilities simultaneously.
We start by putting all states into superposition.
Every state now has the same probability amplitude.
animations: Draw a bar graph with 8 white (#FFFFFF) vertical bars of equal height, labeled |000> through |111> at the base.
Apply a cyan glow (#00FFFF) to all 8 bars simultaneously to represent the state of 'superposition'.
Display the text 'Equal Probability' in light grey (#AAAAAA) above the bars as they pulse.

sections.title: Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)
lecture_lines: The Oracle function marks the correct answer.
It flips the target state's amplitude to negative.
Other amplitudes remain positive and unchanged.
The target is now mathematically distinct from others.
This phase inversion prepares for the next step.
animations: Start with 8 equal white (#FFFFFF) bars; highlight the 6th bar (labeled |101>) in yellow (#FFFF00).
Draw the target icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/target.svg] above the yellow bar to represent the Oracle's identification.
Rotate the yellow bar 180 degrees downward across the X-axis to show negative amplitude.
Keep the other 7 bars stationary and white (#FFFFFF) while the target bar stays yellow and inverted.
Fade in a negative sign '-' in yellow (#FFFF00) next to the inverted bar.

sections.title: Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Inversion about the Mean)
lecture_lines: Calculate the average height of all amplitudes.
Reflect every amplitude across this average line.
The negative target amplitude shoots up high.
Wrong answers shrink closer to zero height.
This is the power of amplitude amplification.
animations: Draw a horizontal dashed line in orange (#FF8C00) across the graph representing the average height of all bars.
Animate each bar moving to its reflected position across the orange dashed line.
The inverted yellow bar (#FFFF00) shoots upward, becoming significantly taller than its original positive height.
The 7 white bars (#FFFFFF) move downward, shrinking to a much smaller height near the X-axis.
Highlight the target bar's peak with a white flash (#FFFFFF) to emphasize 'Amplitude Amplification'.

sections.title: Iteration and Measurement
lecture_lines: Repeat these steps approximately square root N times.
The target amplitude becomes nearly 100 percent.
Measuring the system reveals the needle immediately.
animations: Show a circular 'repeat' icon in light grey (#AAAAAA) while the yellow target bar (#FFFF00) pulses and grows taller.
Animate the target bar (#FFFF00) reaching near-maximum height while all other bars shrink to nearly zero.
A measurement meter icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/meter.svg] appears; all bars vanish except the target bar which turns solid green (#00FF00).
